Based on the search results, I found information about Colorado Revised Statute § 39-22-2003, which addresses state sales tax refunds:

Under this statute, for taxable years beginning January 1, 1999 and each subsequent year, qualified individuals are allowed a state sales tax refund if there were excess state revenues for the fiscal year ending in that tax year.

The refund is triggered when there are excess state revenues for the fiscal year ending in that tax year that voters statewide have not authorized the state to retain and spend and that are required to be refunded pursuant to section 20(7)(d) of article X of the state constitution.

The refund amount varies based on the taxpayer's adjusted gross income, with different percentages applied to different income brackets. For example, individuals with AGI of $25,000 or less receive 25% of the excess state revenues divided by the estimated number of qualifying individuals, while those with AGI over $125,000 receive 15% of the excess state revenues divided by the same denominator.

If the refund allowed under this section exceeds the income taxes otherwise due on the claimant's income, the excess amount shall be refunded to the claimant.
